The Missing Piece#139.src: Oh, you know I didn't mean it like that.

The Missing Piece#140.src: For each year that passes... this tree will grow taller, and ever more beautiful.

The Missing Piece#141.src: It'll have to weather many storms, and on some days it might even have to go without water. And still, it will continue growing.

The Missing Piece#143.src: And then in ten, fifteen, maybe even twenty-five years... we'll finally be able to rest in its shade.

The Missing Piece#144.src: Twenty-five years!? We'll be old by then!
The Missing Piece#144.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#145.src: Oh, I know! We could have a picnic underneath its canopy Doesn't that sound nice, {u}?
The Missing Piece#145.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#146.src: ... It does. It does sound nice, Elise. Perhaps we could.

The Missing Piece#147.src: Go on, give it some more water. Or it'll never grow an inch!

The Missing Piece#152.src: I was just thinking... If I were to die some day, I'd like to be buried here, under the tree.

The Missing Piece#153.src: Huh? What could possibly make you think about such silly things? We still have a long life left ahead of us, don't we?
The Missing Piece#153.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#154.src: Of course, you're right. I'm sorry, I'm just not used to this...

The Missing Piece#157.src: Let's just enjoy the sun, for a bit. There's still work tomorrow.
The Missing Piece#157.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#160.src: Hm. I shall leave the worrying for another day, I think. Today is a good day... not a day for worrying.
The Missing Piece#160.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#161.src: In fact, today is too nice a day to waste it... by not going anywhere, that is. Wouldn't you agree?
The Missing Piece#161.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#163.src: Follow Elise to the roof at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Missing Piece#164.src: Ah... Do you see that factory off that way? I used to work there, back when I was younger...
The Missing Piece#164.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#165.src: We mass-produced bread for the higher regions... Tedious work, and thankless too.
The Missing Piece#165.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#166.src: I'm sure you have noticed, but things around here aren't too easy. Some people even go as far as stealing when times are tough...
The Missing Piece#166.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#167.src: Fortunately... I never had to. They would let us take some home, every once in a while.
The Missing Piece#167.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#168.src: Those were good days. On those occasions, we'd go and have ourselves a picnic, me and- hm. Just me, I suppose.
The Missing Piece#168.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#169.src: A shame it's so hard to come by... the thefts became a real problem, you know. The Crown ended up building a vault down under the factory to keep it all secure!
The Missing Piece#169.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#170.src: How long, since I last had some? Years, surely... not like any of that bread ever makes it to us poor folk, ha!
The Missing Piece#170.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#171.src: But it'd be nice to have some again, I suppose... reminisce on old times.
The Missing Piece#171.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#172.src: Well, if you're running errands for me already... mind seeing if you can get your hands on a loaf or two?
The Missing Piece#172.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#173.src: It's expensive, but for the right price... I'm sure you could get ahold of some. You don't seem the sort to struggle with that kind of thing, do you, letter carrier?
The Missing Piece#173.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#174.src: Ha! Well, do your best, either way. Once you come back, I have a plan for what we can do today. How's that sound?
The Missing Piece#174.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#175.src: Try to enter the Bread Factory at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Missing Piece#176.src: Oh, no... You know! You know! Speak to that constable first, and perhaps, I'll tell you more.
The Missing Piece#176.speaker: Bush

The Missing Piece#177.src: If you've come to beg, you might as well leave.
The Missing Piece#177.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#178.src: Huh? Alright, bud. We all do.
The Missing Piece#178.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#180.src: Do I look like a vending machine to you? Go find somewhere else. We just make bread here, we don't sell it.
The Missing Piece#180.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#181.src: Get out of here pal, you shouldn't be loitering around under a Constable's watch.
The Missing Piece#181.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#182.src: But, but, but! No buts. Don't make me have to do something! The paperwork is always such a hassle...
The Missing Piece#182.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#184.src: Obviously not... We have enough problems as it is, what with that stolen barrel last week... And the production quotas...
The Missing Piece#184.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#185.src: Don't you have something better to do anyway?
The Missing Piece#185.speaker: Constable

The Missing Piece#187.src: Over here, friend of a friend!

The Missing Piece#189.src: Did you know? Did you know? There is more than one way to enter any building.
The Missing Piece#189.speaker: Bush

The Missing Piece#190.src: I'll tell you! But, stealing is unethical, you must know!
The Missing Piece#190.speaker: Bush

The Missing Piece#191.src: As long as she doesn't know! She won't know! Do you understand?
The Missing Piece#191.speaker: Bush

The Missing Piece#192.src: It's just around the corner, you see. A pipe! Now you know! Now you know!
The Missing Piece#192.speaker: Bush

The Missing Piece#193.src: Enter the Bread Factory through the pipe at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Missing Piece#194.src: It's just around the corner, you see. A pipe! Now you know! Now you know!
The Missing Piece#194.speaker: Bush

The Missing Piece#481.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#482.src: Elise. You're- please, forgive me- you're in danger. I-

The Missing Piece#483.src: I'm in danger? I'm just an ordinary worker, what reason would anyone have to harm me? I'll be fine.
The Missing Piece#483.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#484.src: {u}, you're the one pushing herself through this weather, clearly panicking...
The Missing Piece#484.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#485.src: I barely get to see you anymore. And now, out of nowhere, you're here in this state... What's going on? Please, just talk to me.
The Missing Piece#485.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#486.src: ...ha. I- I haven't been truthful with you, Elise, and- I can explain later. We need to get out of here, before they-

The Missing Piece#489.src: Why would they... no, this doesn't make any sense...

The Missing Piece#490.src: Hm. Well, then maybe it's nothing. I'll go see who it is.
The Missing Piece#490.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#491.src: As if one wasn't enough... who could possibly be foolish enough to brave a storm just to come visit this little place? Whatever it is, it can wait.
The Missing Piece#491.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#494.src: No... No... What are you... Why are you-
The Missing Piece#494.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#495.src: Apologies for the disturbance, madam. But I'm afraid we have business to attend to.
The Missing Piece#495.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#497.src: {u}, {u}, why are they here? Why... why won't you answer me...?
The Missing Piece#497.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#498.src: What have you done? I... Please, just explain... I- I...
The Missing Piece#498.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#499.src: I... how did I overlook this...?

The Missing Piece#500.src: Seems you're not quite the strategic mastermind you though yourself, Lioness.
The Missing Piece#500.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#502.src: Elise... if you... if you just cooperate...

The Missing Piece#503.src: Then... everything will be fine. It... it will.

The Missing Piece#506.src: She... What did she do? Why did she wrap me up in it?
The Missing Piece#506.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#507.src: Everything I remember... it just leaves me with more questions than answers. Why can't I remember her...? Why!?
The Missing Piece#507.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#508.src: I- I'm just an ordinary factory worker! I woke up early, worked late, slept late... then did it all over again the next day.
The Missing Piece#508.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#509.src: I've never said a word about the Crown! Why would they possibly care about... me...?
The Missing Piece#509.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#510.src: They... they took everything from me. My youth, my body, my time, and... and I never demanded anything in return.
The Missing Piece#510.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#511.src: So, why... why can't I just have this? This one little thing? Why can't I remember her...?
The Missing Piece#511.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#512.src: ...oh, it might sound sad... but, looking back at it all like this...
The Missing Piece#512.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#513.src: My life doesn't seem all that great, does it? Ha. Toiling away in a factory for someone else's bread...
The Missing Piece#513.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#514.src: But I can feel her. Even if... even if I can't remember her face, or her name, or her touch... I still feel her. Lingering in my heart. Shining.
The Missing Piece#514.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#515.src: ...it's all some sort of sick joke, isn't it?
The Missing Piece#515.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#516.src: They weren't content with all I sacrificed... they had to take even my memories? Is that it...?
The Missing Piece#516.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#518.src: Wherever you are now... whatever you did... whatever secrets you kept... I hope it was worth it.
The Missing Piece#518.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#519.src: I hope you burn this entire place to the ground.
The Missing Piece#519.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#521.src: I just wish... we could have spent more time together.
The Missing Piece#521.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#522.src: For a long time, I went along the path that had been laid before me. I did what was right.

The Missing Piece#523.src: But then... I met you, Elise.

The Missing Piece#524.src: I... I don't know what to say, {u}...
The Missing Piece#524.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#527.src: I see... A bird. A pigeon, it's old and gray. Its wings no longer work like they used to...
The Missing Piece#527.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#528.src: It wants to fly, but it can't... It's struggling...
The Missing Piece#528.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#530.src: No, I can't! It's too sad...
The Missing Piece#530.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#532.src: It's sitting beneath the shade of a canopy, singing. Like a cry, almost, mourning.
The Missing Piece#532.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#533.src: The clouds, dark clouds are gathering. A storm is coming. The bird is looking around, frantically searching. It's scared.
The Missing Piece#533.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#534.src: It... It calls out, for something... or someone...
The Missing Piece#534.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#535.src: Who is it calling for, Elise?

The Missing Piece#540.src: I won't forget! I won't forget! I won't! I promised! I promised I'd never forget you!
The Missing Piece#540.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#543.src: You are an ordinary worker from the Roughworks. You work an ordinary job, and lead an ordinary but solitary life.
The Missing Piece#543.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#545.src: She is nothing to you. You have never met her. You will never meet her.
The Missing Piece#545.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#548.src: You are nothing to her! She is nothing to you! Soon you'll forget she ever existed.
The Missing Piece#548.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#549.src: No, I will never forget! She was everything to me! She is everything to me! I will never forget her!
The Missing Piece#549.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#550.src: She is nothing to you. You have never met her. You will never meet her.
The Missing Piece#550.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#551.src: You do not know her face, nor her voice, nor her touch.
The Missing Piece#551.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#553.src: She is nothing to you. You have never met her. You will never meet her. You have always been ordinary, you will always be ordinary.
The Missing Piece#553.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#556.src: I will ask once more. Is your directive understood?
The Missing Piece#556.speaker: Inquisitor

The Missing Piece#567.src: And I'll never forget it, Elise.
The Missing Piece#567.speaker: Syndra

The Missing Piece#570.src: My legs... feel funny... I think... I think I'm in need of some rest. A long, long rest... I deserve that... don't I?
The Missing Piece#570.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#571.src: You'll take me home... won't you? I want to see it, at least once more... The tree.
The Missing Piece#571.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#575.src: It's grown so tall... and so beautiful. Hasn't it, Syndra...?
The Missing Piece#575.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#576.src: If... If only... you could have seen it... like this...
The Missing Piece#576.speaker: Elise

The Missing Piece#579.src: Pick some of Elise's flowers around her house at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Olmic Rune#001.src: Find some sort of fuel in the Ruined City.
The Olmic Rune#001.dst: 在 Ruined City 裡找到某種燃料。

The Olmic Rune#002.src: Explore the cave for the fuel

The Olmic Rune#003.src: Collect [{~} Fuel Sprites] and bring it back to the machine.
The Olmic Rune#003.dst: 收集 [{~} Fuel Sprites] 帶回機器那裡。

The Olmic Rune#004.src: Head back to the machine at [{~},-{~}]

The Olmic Rune#005.src: Defend the machine from the incoming attackers.
The Olmic Rune#005.dst: 守住機器，擋下來襲的敵人。

The Order of the Grook#000.src: Talk to Seasum in a tower on {p}.

The Order of the Grook#001.src: Ugh... I really, really, reeeeally don't want to go...
The Order of the Grook#001.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#003.src: Do you... not have manners at all?! Just running into my parents' house like that! Jeez!
The Order of the Grook#003.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#005.src: Oh, I know! Here, go to my room real fast, and grab the letter in there
The Order of the Grook#005.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#006.src: Bring it back to me when you do, I wanna make sure it's the right one.
The Order of the Grook#006.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#007.src: Get the school invitation from Seasum room and bring it to Seasum.

The Order of the Grook#008.src: Yep, that's the right letter. I hope you like school!
The Order of the Grook#008.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#009.src: My parents were super exited when that letter flew into my room, but magical school sounds so boring...
The Order of the Grook#009.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#010.src: I don't even want to learn magic! I just want to write my stories and play games. You can go instead.
The Order of the Grook#010.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#011.src: I know the picture on the letter is of me, but you can, um...
The Order of the Grook#011.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#012.src: You can say you had a growth spurt! Uh, that should work, i think!
The Order of the Grook#012.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#013.src: Now go on, you should get out before my parents see you. I don't want them to find out I gave that letter away...
The Order of the Grook#013.speaker: Seasum

The Order of the Grook#014.src: Talk to the School Ship Captain on the pier next to the Seaskipper Captain.

The Order of the Grook#015.src: Hey! What are you doing all the way over here? This dock's broken.
The Order of the Grook#015.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#016.src: Oh, a student, you say. Aren't you a little old to be learning fundamental magical knowledge?
The Order of the Grook#016.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#017.src: Well, if I could see your invitation letter, then?
The Order of the Grook#017.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#018.src: ...Hm. This...wow, you really look quite different than the picture. Did you get a new haircut?
The Order of the Grook#018.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#019.src: Well, no judging from me! Keep walking to the end of the dock. Have faith!
The Order of the Grook#019.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#021.src: Alright everyone. Ready for a magical experience?
The Order of the Grook#021.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#022.src: We're headed to the Nexus. You've been told where to go. If you've forgotten, ask your fellow students!
The Order of the Grook#022.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#023.src: If you ever need to come back here, just walk out onto the dock again. Good luck, now!
The Order of the Grook#023.speaker: Boat Captain

The Order of the Grook#024.src: Follow the children to the school.

The Order of the Grook#025.src: Through the wall, right? I hope my uniform doesn't get dirty.
The Order of the Grook#025.speaker: Student

The Order of the Grook#026.src: Talk to Cidre on the school island.

The Order of the Grook#028.src: Welcome to the island of Grookwarts! I will be guiding and helping all the new students.
The Order of the Grook#028.speaker: Cidre

The Order of the Grook#029.src: So all of you will be getting two vouchers each, and with them you will need to buy one wand and a book or tome.
The Order of the Grook#029.speaker: Cidre

The Order of the Grook#030.src: You can find everything here around the docks. Choosing your materials is very important, so buy the ones that speak to you!
The Order of the Grook#030.speaker: Cidre

The Order of the Grook#031.src: When you're done, meet with Miss Una at the front gates!
The Order of the Grook#031.speaker: Cidre

The Order of the Grook#032.src: Purchase a wand from the Wand Merchant and a book from the Magical Book Merchant, then talk to Una.

The Order of the Grook#034.src: Seems like you all have your materials in order. You are now free to enter Grookwarts and begin your lessons.
The Order of the Grook#034.speaker: Una

The Order of the Grook#035.src: The door is just behind me. Walk on in!
The Order of the Grook#035.speaker: Una

The Order of the Grook#036.src: Attend the welcoming dinner at Grookwarts.

The Order of the Grook#037.src: Hush, hush! The speech will be soon!
The Order of the Grook#037.speaker: Student

The Order of the Grook#038.src: Hurry, take a seat! The banquet will be starting any second now!
The Order of the Grook#038.speaker: Student

The Order of the Grook#039.src: Magical children of Wynn and Gavel alike... We welcome you here, to our fair academy.

The Order of the Grook#040.src: Oh lordy, the headmaster! I didn't even see him come in!
The Order of the Grook#040.speaker: Student

The Order of the Grook#041.src: Uhm... I don't see him at all, actually...
The Order of the Grook#041.speaker: Student

The Order of the Grook#042.src: Well, I should hope you can see me now, all of you. Oh, what a splendid turnout this year!
The Order of the Grook#042.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#043.src: Apologies, I simply can't resist a bit of theatrics. But now, it is time to listen and learn, fledgeling Grooks.
The Order of the Grook#043.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#044.src: We knowledged mages and scholars, the Order of the Grook, are pleased to see each of you here. Whether you be a young mind aching with curiosity...
The Order of the Grook#044.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#045.src: ...or an old hat looking to refine their knowledge, all seeking to learn magic are welcomed here. We expect great things of you.
The Order of the Grook#045.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#046.src: Now, to business. You will write your schedules for the semester. Look down on your paper and write in what classes you wish to participate in.
The Order of the Grook#046.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#047.src: You will need to choose four classes, one from each category. The categories are: Elemental Magic, Practical Magic, Magical Creatures, and Types of magic.
The Order of the Grook#047.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#048.src: The schedule book is at the end of the table. Worry not, there is no limit on class size. If you wish to take it, you may take it.
The Order of the Grook#048.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#050.src: Talk to the Ghost Guide and attend your chosen classes (The Ghost Guide will lead you to each class):

The Order of the Grook#051.src: I'll be leading you to your classes, everyone! Talk to me when you're ready to go.
The Order of the Grook#051.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#052.src: Alright, fledgeling Grooks! Your first class is starting in just a minute. Follow me!
The Order of the Grook#052.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#053.src: Here are the elemental classes. Step on in. Your magical journey truly begins here!
The Order of the Grook#053.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#054.src: Now, all of you. Sit. Listen.
The Order of the Grook#054.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#055.src: Earth is an element of great power. Versatile and everpresent, nearly as the air.
The Order of the Grook#055.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#056.src: Thunder provides force... Earth provides sheer power. The difference... Force choose its own path. Power is force, directed.
The Order of the Grook#056.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#057.src: Earth is also the earth itself. Stone, metal, trees and soil. Trees sway in the wind, but do not break. And the mountains do not crumble.
The Order of the Grook#057.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#058.src: The Touroto, stepped in earthly magic, are nearly invincible to all but themselves. It is proof of the earth's strength.
The Order of the Grook#058.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#059.src: The Doguns... They were masters of the earth, and fire alike, shaping caverns to their will... And now, nearly extinct. A terrible crime...
The Order of the Grook#059.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#060.src: But we shall honor them, and move forwards. We shall strike the earth and claim it to be our own.
The Order of the Grook#060.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#061.src: The tome directs the earth's force. Take it and utilize it to shatter the stones I summon.
The Order of the Grook#061.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#062.src: The darkest parts of the stones are weak points. Find them, and learn the power of the earth.
The Order of the Grook#062.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#063.src: You know the earth's power, fledgeling. There is nothing more for you here. Go.
The Order of the Grook#063.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#064.src: Hee hee, take your seats, take your seats, TAKE. YOUR. SEATS. A marvelous batch of eager students today!!
The Order of the Grook#064.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#065.src: Almost as marvelous as the powers of Thunder! Energy! Pure, unfocused energy! Devastation, desolation, industrialization all alike!
The Order of the Grook#065.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#066.src: Yes, yes! Thunder is technical and versatile! Unreliable to all those who don't know how to rely on it, to those dexterous of hand and mind!
The Order of the Grook#066.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#067.src: But woe, woe, Thunder is reviled, reviled! Pure energy has no morality! If used for good, yes yes, ho hum, but if used for evil, oh, burn the witch! Burn, burn! Evil, they say! Pah!!
The Order of the Grook#067.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#068.src: All magicks are unaligned with silly concepts such as morality. They are pure chaos! But Thunder, the element of energy and force, it seems ever so EASY to use for evil...
The Order of the Grook#068.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#069.src: And evil has found it, found it! CORRUPTION!! DEMONS!! Forces anathema to us, but knowleged in the ways of force and thus, thunder! So terrible, terrible, and thunder mages feared, feared...
The Order of the Grook#069.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#070.src: And then, then! Joyous day, the Corkians arrived with their marvelous machines, and their electromagic! Thunder controlled, thunder tamed! The wonder of it all!
The Order of the Grook#070.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#071.src: Electromagic makes handles crank, gears spin, metal move, gives sheer stones the power to THINK, and to PLAN! A Corkian original, and a splendid, splendid development reintroduced!
The Order of the Grook#071.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#072.src: And so, you shall see for yourselves! Electromagic at work! You will control thunder and electricity, and make the machines bend to your world today, today, this shocking day!
The Order of the Grook#072.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#073.src: The mechanism is behind me now! Come up, come up! See the power of thunder, shackled by our whims, won't you, {u}?
The Order of the Grook#073.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#074.src: Whee hee hee! Thunder tamed, thunder shackled, and your magical wings unbound by such petty concepts, {u}! What a show!
The Order of the Grook#074.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#075.src: Expand your knowledge ever further, further! Your task is complete, complete, and your next awaits!
The Order of the Grook#075.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#076.src: Aah, wow! Everyone s-sure got here quick...
The Order of the Grook#076.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#077.src: Welcome, w-welcome. The Water element class is...certainly an interesting one, I-I'd hope... Because water doesn't j-just pertain to, well, w-water...
The Order of the Grook#077.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#078.src: It also the element o-of knowledge, and pure magicality. Water i-is sort of magical default, If you w-will. If it isn't focused on on o-one element or another, magic ends up being water-based
The Order of the Grook#078.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#079.src: Learning a-about the water element and e-expanding your horizons can allow you to cast spells easier... C-control the flow of magic better, you see.
The Order of the Grook#079.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#080.src: Most aquatic creatures are t-tied to water, though creatures that live in icy or snowy environments are, t-too...often, they are also connected to air, but not always.
The Order of the Grook#080.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#081.src: In a-addition, many holy artifacts are enchanted with water magic... S-something about how it's a pure type of energy, I believe.
The Order of the Grook#081.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#082.src: Lastly, healing abilities are b-bolstered by water magic. Just knowing magic well d-doesn't help, but actually having artifacts charged w-with water magic can increase healing capabilities.
The Order of the Grook#082.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#083.src: N-now, for your test, I have...um, a...a test. Anyone who wants to try it f-first, just go up and start.
The Order of the Grook#083.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#084.src: Good w-work there! I h-hope it wasn't too boring with my talking... You can go now.
The Order of the Grook#084.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#085.src: N-now, who's n-next? And... i-is it really cold in here for all of you, too? Or, is it j-just me?
The Order of the Grook#085.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#086.src: Good to see a decent turnout this year for my class. Too dangerous, pah! You can take this just fine.
The Order of the Grook#086.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#087.src: Anyways. The fire element class. Many misunderstand just what fire stands for... but after today, you will leave with courage in your hearts.
The Order of the Grook#087.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#088.src: Fire is, of course, related to physical fire, magma, etcetera. A burning torch is a source of fire magic, but that is not the only source of it.
The Order of the Grook#088.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#089.src: Courage, bravery, and defensiveness are also tied to the fire element. Those stalwart and selfless, willing to sacrifice themselves for others.
The Order of the Grook#089.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#090.src: In addition, water is tied to healing magic, fire is tied to self-healing. Regenerative capacity if you will. Many fire-based artifacts heal the user passively.
The Order of the Grook#090.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#091.src: And while they are on the verge of extinction after the war in the {p}, the Dogun species used to embody fire and earth magic alike. It is a shame what happened to them.
The Order of the Grook#091.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#092.src: Unfortunately, it is also notable that corrupted creatures are often connected to fire, by nature of the corruption seeming to bring heat wherever it goes...
The Order of the Grook#092.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#093.src: But aside from that, onto our practical test. You will all come up to me, starting with {u}, and hone courage. I will be casting balls of fire at you.
The Order of the Grook#093.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#094.src: You will need to dodge these fire charges. If you are hit, it counts as a failure. Now. Let's get started, {u}.
The Order of the Grook#094.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#095.src: Are you ready? Summon your bravery.
The Order of the Grook#095.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#096.src: Well done {u}, fledgeling Grook! Continue to sharpen your instincts. You'll be a fine hero someday, I am sure of it.
The Order of the Grook#096.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#097.src: Dismissed, {u}. You may leave. Now do I have any volunteers for the next round...?
The Order of the Grook#097.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#098.src: Arright class, the sooner we start, the sooner we finish, so everyone, take your seats! You'll be getting up soon enough anyways!
The Order of the Grook#098.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#099.src: Movin' right along. Air! You're breathing it, we're surrounded by it, but ain'tcha know what it's all about yet, so pay attention.
The Order of the Grook#099.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#100.src: Air is an element of freedom! speed, wind and agility. if you're trained well with agility, attacks'll seem like they just phase through ya!
The Order of the Grook#100.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#101.src: But over and above that, 'cause of air's ever-presence, it's one of the most versatile kinda magic in existence. People use it in all sorts of ways.
The Order of the Grook#101.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#102.src: Over in Gavel, the Bantisu Air Monks have managed to extend their sight by the wind! They use it to help guide folks who get lost in that canyon over there.
The Order of the Grook#102.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#103.src: Many winged sorts a'creatures are tied to air, but not all of them. Some magic users just straight-out float! Now wouldn't that be nice, eh?
The Order of the Grook#103.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#104.src: Due to their tenuous physicality, souls and spirits are also often related to air magic. Make ya wonder if you could just blow ghost out of the window!
The Order of the Grook#104.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#105.src: And finally, some old, old tales tell of a woman who crossed the sea before it was calmed using air magic to fly. 's just an old legend, but an interesting one.
The Order of the Grook#105.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#106.src: Now onto the practical test! It's time to get those bones a-shakin'! You'll be running an obstacle course I have set up, but with a twist.
The Order of the Grook#106.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#107.src: Everyone up to the table! You'll need this feather with ya to get through.It'll help you jump higher!
The Order of the Grook#107.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#108.src: The goal is to grab three crystal balls I put in the obstacle course. once you found 'em, bring 'em back to me.
The Order of the Grook#108.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#109.src: The course is behind me. Shake a leg now!
The Order of the Grook#109.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#110.src: Lessee here, one, two, three, yes indeedy! You got through that pretty quick!
The Order of the Grook#110.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#111.src: Now, if you'll just hand me back that feather ya got there...
The Order of the Grook#111.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#112.src: ...then you'll be all done! Congrats, little fledge, you've finished this class! Now get on along to your next one!
The Order of the Grook#112.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#113.src: Moving swiftly on, the next class is just across the way. Follow me!
The Order of the Grook#113.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#114.src: Alright everyone. Take a seat but don't get comfy. You'll be getting up soon. Hope you brought your reading glasses
The Order of the Grook#114.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#115.src: See, I'll just be giving you short primer, then sending you out for the practical exercise, Since I have all this written down already.
The Order of the Grook#115.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#116.src: The basis of this class is that many materials, whether you know it or not, are inherently magical in some way or another. If you want to be artificer, you need to know how each one works.
The Order of the Grook#116.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#117.src: Thankfully, the field of artifice is very popular one, so there's a wealth of knowledge out there on magical materials and how to use them efficiently.
The Order of the Grook#117.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#118.src: Heck, Wynn soldiers are cobbling together rings out of copper and old spider silk, so you know this sort of thing is easy to get to. Tough to master, though!
The Order of the Grook#118.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#119.src: For those intimidated, you don't need much crafting knowledge for this class; you'll be reading up on everything you need to know in the back.
The Order of the Grook#119.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#120.src: You all be crafting a magical amulet using different items. I've stockpiled in the back; everyone will be crafting a different kind of necklace.
The Order of the Grook#120.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#121.src: Here's a note on what you should craft. Once you have the materials you think you need, come to the crafting table. It's enchanted, and will craft the item for you if you have what you need.
The Order of the Grook#121.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#122.src: Mhm, that's the ticket, {u}. If you're interested in learning more, you can probably find my books in most of the libraries.
The Order of the Grook#122.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#123.src: Your feathers are coming out just nicely, fledgeling. You can scoot off to your next class now
The Order of the Grook#123.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#124.src: Okay class, everyone take your seats, and listen up. This class is going to be interesting.
The Order of the Grook#124.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#125.src: As you know, this class is all about magical effects, specifically those tied to various materials, and how they'll affect you!
The Order of the Grook#125.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#126.src: This is going to be a hands-on learning experience, so those of you with weak constitutions may request to skip the demonstration if you're concerned for your health.
The Order of the Grook#126.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#127.src: If you've read my books, you know about Quartz, and how dangerous it can be if overcharged. So, of course, we have overcharged sample so you can feel the signs of it.
The Order of the Grook#127.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#128.src: It may be explosive, but it will be in a controlled manner. The worst that'll happen to you is your face will get a bit dusty, or your glasses will fall off.
The Order of the Grook#128.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#129.src: Magical crystals, as we have to my left here, can be charged with all kinds of different effects. This is an incredibly valuable aspect for artificers.
The Order of the Grook#129.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#130.src: Depending on the formation, they can have natural effects as well. These crystals were found in Gavel's flouting islands, and...well, let's say it's difficult to keep it in its case.
The Order of the Grook#130.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#131.src: Our last sample is of cosmic material, and if you're sickened easily, then don't examine it. Its effects are mostly unknown, but one thing's certain...
The Order of the Grook#131.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#132.src: ...it's dangerous to be exposed for long periods. Now, each of you will go back behind me, and examine and interact with each of the three samples provided.
The Order of the Grook#132.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#133.src: Once you've done so, then you can leave. Hands-on training is the best way to learn, after all.
The Order of the Grook#133.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#134.src: Well done. How did that feel?
The Order of the Grook#134.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#135.src: Personally, the void sample is the most interesting to me. You may now leave the classroom.
The Order of the Grook#135.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#136.src: There's a bit of a walk to your next class. Follow me.
The Order of the Grook#136.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#137.src: These staircases were supposed to move, but... That was too much work to put together, apparently. They're a pain to navigate, aren't they?
The Order of the Grook#137.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#138.src: Alright, fledgeling grooks. Time to hit you all with the info you're really here for!
The Order of the Grook#138.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#139.src: Wybels! Pronounced like nibble, they're a rather popular pet nowadays. But you all knew that, you want to know where they came from.
The Order of the Grook#139.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#140.src: The explanation we got was that they lived in the Ahms region, and when it split open, they eventually burrowed into the surface of the {p}.
The Order of the Grook#140.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#141.src: But no one actually KNOWS for sure. That means they. Could. Be. ANYTHING! What could lie beneath that veneer of fluff and playful demeanor?!
The Order of the Grook#141.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#142.src: Oh, speaking of fluff. The wooly fur never actually stops growing, ever, and neither do their hooves, their horns, or their teeth. They shed often.
The Order of the Grook#142.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#143.src: These materials have innate magical energy to them. Stable like lodestone and reliable like quartz, but not as powerful as either. Interesting, that a fluffball has that potential!!
The Order of the Grook#143.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#144.src: Wybel fluff is also able to be boiled, and it turns into sticky molasses-like substance. It's used for candy, and its very popular...but it's all POISON!!
The Order of the Grook#144.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#145.src: It's POISON, I tell you! Wyble meat is horrendously inedible! It'll give you the worst stomachache of your life! The candymakers are feeding us DEATH!
The Order of the Grook#145.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#146.src: And the worst part is, if too much fluff gathers up in one spot, ANOTHER WYBEL APPEARS! They reproduce by budding!! Growing out of lint and dust! It's a no-win game they're makin' us play!
The Order of the Grook#146.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#147.src: Wybels do have some good use though...they can sniff out sources of cosmic magic, like a pig sniffs out truffles. Sometimes they even try to take it home.
The Order of the Grook#147.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#148.src: It's almost like they miss it, somehow. It's almost like they might be FROM outer space! It's ALMOST like they bringing insanity-inducing things into our houses ON PURPOSE!
The Order of the Grook#148.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#149.src: They're here to kill us all, I swear it! How else would you explain a wybel VAPORIZING a group of poachers? Ten colors of wybel, every one of them rotten evil!
The Order of the Grook#149.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#150.src: Everyone says there's only nine, but WE know the truth! There's a tenth out there, an ultimately powerful one that want us all gone. Pray you never see it, kids.
The Order of the Grook#150.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#151.src: Anyways, my lesson's safe from all that. All you have to do is to re-order these plush Wybel toys on the stand. You'll figure out once you're up here.
The Order of the Grook#151.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#152.src: Alrighty, fledgeling, good job. You're armed with the REAL truth now! Go on to your next class.
The Order of the Grook#152.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#153.src: Hello, students. This is the magical creatures class, and I will be your instructor.
The Order of the Grook#153.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#154.src: Different species have different levels of innate magicality. This is often an invisible aspect of the species. You must never assume.
The Order of the Grook#154.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#155.src: To begin with, Doguns. They are ancient creatures, artificial-seeming at first. Despite this, they are highly adept at earth and fire-based magic.
The Order of the Grook#155.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#156.src: Able to quite literally move mountains, it is theorized that they were the one who carve out the inside of the {p} into the caves we know today.
The Order of the Grook#156.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#157.src: Tales also tell of their utilizing demonic energy for various purposes. However, we are only able to assume their magical energy from Dwarven tales, as they are nigh-extinct
The Order of the Grook#157.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#158.src: Moving on. The term "Greenskins" is a catch-all for Trolls, Goblins, Orcs, Ogres and Hobgoblins. Some include Gerts into this definition, though by technicality they are separate.
The Order of the Grook#158.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#159.src: Though many Greenskins societies with mystical particles, the only known way for them to utilize magic is through magical artifacts. They've little magic potential.
The Order of the Grook#159.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#160.src: Meanwhile, Villagers are the opposite persuasion. High magical potential, often unrealized out of laziness.
The Order of the Grook#160.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#161.src: Humans are often thought of as magical then Villagers, due to Fruman soldiers seeming to know some magic innate, but this is untrue.
The Order of the Grook#161.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#162.src: Dwarves have a similar level of magicality to Humans, but like the Villagers, it often go unrealized. Their culture values physical strength more.
The Order of the Grook#162.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#163.src: It is theorized that the reason for this is due to their distance for demonic energies of the Doguns. They reject their magic potential often, such that it is lessening over time.
The Order of the Grook#163.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#164.src: Inversely, Elves have a deep connection to their magicality. Despite their reclusiveness, they are known for their open share of magicality energy within their own society.
The Order of the Grook#164.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#165.src: The outcast Elves of {p} have shared their connection to what we refers to as "The Light". This connection is supposedly unfathomable, but guides them and protects them.
The Order of the Grook#165.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#166.src: Now, we see if you were paying attention. You will come here and order the societies I have referred to in the class from least magical, to the most.
The Order of the Grook#166.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#167.src: Well done, you got it right!
The Order of the Grook#167.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#168.src: Correct. {u}, thank you for paying attention. No one ever seems to in this class. You may go.
The Order of the Grook#168.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#169.src: Next class is actually rather close!
The Order of the Grook#169.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#171.src: ...I was hoping for a smaller class size.
The Order of the Grook#171.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#172.src: Corruption is incredibly dangerous...it'll be tough to keep so many students safe. If anyone wishes to leave, you may.
The Order of the Grook#172.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#173.src: Now... Corruption is a force of nature of...some description. Yes, you heard me right. We don't actually know much about it.
The Order of the Grook#173.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#174.src: Even though it's plagued the Wynn province for a thousand years, the way it behaves is so incredibly alien in nature that it's nigh-impossible to study.
The Order of the Grook#174.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#175.src: We know it raises undead bodies... The working theory is that the more heavily injured a target is, the more susceptible they are to being corrupted.
The Order of the Grook#175.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#176.src: And...well, you can't exactly get more injured than "dead". Hence, the growth of zombies and skeletons and all, over in Wynn.
The Order of the Grook#176.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#177.src: It appears to spread by a complex "root" system. A scientist from {p}, Orikal, has studied this. The corruption spikes appear to spread it in greater concentration.
The Order of the Grook#177.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#178.src: As for the effects on your person, most often paranoia and anger are seen. And that's about the only consistent thing with it; it affect everyone slightly differently.
The Order of the Grook#178.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#179.src: The worst part is that practically everything single thing we've touched on here is conjecture and theorycrafting! The force of corruption is terrifying.
The Order of the Grook#179.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#180.src: The only thing we know for certain is that powerful ice-based magic can halt corruption, as seen in the {p} region.
The Order of the Grook#180.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#181.src: Now, the dangerous part. Everyone, come up past my desk here. We'll examine a corrupted creature in a controlled environment.
The Order of the Grook#181.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#182.src: We have one in captivity, and its cage is reinforced with the strongest metals we have...so dear god let it be enough.
The Order of the Grook#182.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#183.src: Bringing it out now...be sure to back up. We don't want anyone caught in the crossfire here.
The Order of the Grook#183.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#184.src: One thing to note about undead corrupteds...they can't be cured. You can weaken them, but that's about it. ...wait...
The Order of the Grook#184.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#185.src: Wait, why's it spreading here? It's never done this before! E-everyone, back up, now!
The Order of the Grook#185.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#186.src: A-as you can see, corruption is very powerful, eheheh, c-can someone go get another teacher or something?!
The Order of the Grook#186.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#187.src: Wait, no! It's corroding the bars! Everyone, RUN! NOW! GET OUT OF HERE, CLASS DISMISSED!!!
The Order of the Grook#187.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#188.src: GAACK! No, {u}, I said RUN! Don't fight that thing, get OUT!
The Order of the Grook#188.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#189.src: Dear lord...that was awful. {u}, I can't believe you were able to kill that thing!
The Order of the Grook#189.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#190.src: Class absolutely dismissed. We've got to cancel this class...it's far too dangerous for the students...
The Order of the Grook#190.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#191.src: Welcome in, guys and gals... we're learnin' about nature magic today!
The Order of the Grook#191.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#192.src: There's two main ways of usin' nature magic... Shamanism and druidism. Two sides of the same coin, man.
The Order of the Grook#192.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#193.src: Druidic Practices tend to deal with healing more, and nurturing. When life's created, it gives off energy... and Druids use that energy for their magic.
The Order of the Grook#193.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#194.src: Shamanic skills are a lot more direct, man. They take the life from other things and use that to do their stuffs. It's way more varied than Druidic magic.
The Order of the Grook#194.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#195.src: Each has its ups and downs, man. Druidism is chill and helpful... but you can really expand your mind with Shamanism, buddies.
The Order of the Grook#195.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#196.src: Either way, it's all about equivalent exchange, y'see? You can't get somethin' from nothin', man. Either make life or take life.
The Order of the Grook#196.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#197.src: But! It's not peaky about what life you take, man! A good shaman takes from plants and animals, not people!
The Order of the Grook#197.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#198.src: Don't be a Slykaar, kiddos. He asked for human sacrifices, but he lived in a jungle, man! Like, what the hey! He coulda done anything alse!
The Order of the Grook#198.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#199.src: Anyways, our test today, little buds, is to practice some shamanic skills. We got a sick cow in the back, and you're gonna nurse it back to health.
The Order of the Grook#199.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#200.src: You'll need to sacrifice some old grooks, but it has to be just the right amount, man! The practice is through the door behind me.
The Order of the Grook#200.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#201.src: Groovy work, man! You're at one with nature!
The Order of the Grook#201.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#202.src: Your feathers are all grown out, man! Time to head out!
The Order of the Grook#202.speaker: Teacher

The Order of the Grook#204.src: That's all four classes! I hope you found them magically enriching! Now, off to the graduation hall!
The Order of the Grook#204.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#205.src: It's the room all the way at the bottom of the stairs. Hurry, don't hold up the ceremony! It won't start until everyone's there.
The Order of the Grook#205.speaker: Ghost Guide

The Order of the Grook#206.src: Go to the ceremony room for the Headmaster's closing speech.

The Order of the Grook#207.src: Take a seat. The ceremony is starting.
The Order of the Grook#207.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#208.src: And so, your teachings, or at least their basics, have ended. Your magical feathers have started to grow!
The Order of the Grook#208.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#209.src: You have all been performing very well during your classes today. I've heard quite a bit of praise from the teachers being passed around.
The Order of the Grook#209.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#210.src: But now, for your efforts, you shall not go unrewarded. You will leave here with more than simply knowledge.
The Order of the Grook#210.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#211.src: Your tools have shaped your minds, subtly but inexorably. And so with that, what you leave with today, both in mind and in treasure, shall be different for each of you.
The Order of the Grook#211.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#212.src: Let us start with . Please come up to the stage!
The Order of the Grook#212.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#213.src: There is a reason I've called you up first, you know. Recall what I said about old hats earlier? Don't think we didn't notice the armor, or the weapon, or the grim countenance.
The Order of the Grook#213.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#214.src: But no need to worry. Those who truly have the drive to become learned in the ways of magic, no matter who they are, will always find their way here, and be accepted.
The Order of the Grook#214.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#215.src: A shame about Seasum, but not to worry. Now, hand over your materials, and you'll receive your rewards.
The Order of the Grook#215.speaker: Headmaster

The Order of the Grook#216.src: And there you have it. Your feathers are grown, and you can spread your magical wings! Good luck on your adventures, Wynn soldier.
The Order of the Grook#216.speaker: Headmaster

The Passage (Quest)#002.src: My dad said I can't let any strangers through this passage!
The Passage (Quest)#002.dst: 我爸說了，我不能讓任何陌生人通過這條通道！
The Passage (Quest)#002.speaker: Wirt

The Passage (Quest)#003.src: If you want access, talk to him, he's the recruiter of the town! His name is Ildan. He's just southwest of here.
The Passage (Quest)#003.dst: 你要想過去，去找他談。他是鎮上的招募官！他叫 Ildan，就在這裡的西南邊。
The Passage (Quest)#003.speaker: Wirt

The Passage (Quest)#004.src: Find Ildan in {p} at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}] and ask to be a member of the town
The Passage (Quest)#004.dst: 在 {p} 的 [-{~1}, {~2}, -{~3}] 找到 Ildan，請求成為鎮上的一員

The Passage (Quest)#005.src: Oh! So you want to become a member of this town?
The Passage (Quest)#005.dst: 哦！所以你想成為這個鎮的一員？
The Passage (Quest)#005.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#006.src: You will have to help us first, of course!
The Passage (Quest)#006.dst: 那當然得先幫我們一個忙！
The Passage (Quest)#006.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#007.src: I'm sure you've noticed, but there is a tribe camp not too far from here.
The Passage (Quest)#007.dst: 你應該注意到了，離這裡不遠有個部落營地。
The Passage (Quest)#007.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#008.src: They used to have a powerful chief, but he eventually died in battle.
The Passage (Quest)#008.dst: 他們以前有位很強的酋長，後來戰死了。
The Passage (Quest)#008.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#009.src: The tribe couldn't bear the fact that he was dead. They performed some unethical necromancy spell on him.
The Passage (Quest)#009.dst: 部落無法接受他的死，於是對他施了某種不該碰的死靈術。
The Passage (Quest)#009.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#010.src: They quickly realized that is was a bad idea, so they locked him in a tomb.
The Passage (Quest)#010.dst: 他們很快就發現這是個爛主意，所以把他鎖進了一座墓穴。
The Passage (Quest)#010.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#011.src: He keeps reviving his minions and it's causing quite some problems to our army.
The Passage (Quest)#011.dst: 他不斷把手下復活，給我們的軍隊帶來不少麻煩。
The Passage (Quest)#011.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#012.src: You can access the tomb from a sacrificial shrine, I've heard, but I'm not sure how. There are probably hints nearby the shrine.
The Passage (Quest)#012.dst: 我聽說可以從一座獻祭神壇進入那座墓穴，但我不確定怎麼進。神壇附近應該會有提示。
The Passage (Quest)#012.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#013.src: Bring me back [{~} Antic Bead] as a proof of its death, and I will let you become a citizen.
The Passage (Quest)#013.dst: 把 [{~} 古怪珠子] 帶回來給我當作牠已死的憑證，我就讓你成為鎮民。
The Passage (Quest)#013.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#014.src: I've marked the direction to the shrine in your book. Remember, there should be hints right nearby the shrine. Good luck.
The Passage (Quest)#014.dst: 我把神壇的方向標在你的書上了。記住，提示就在神壇附近。祝你好運。
The Passage (Quest)#014.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#015.src: Search for clues near [-{~}, {~}, -{~}] and bring back [{~} Antic Bead] to Ildan.
The Passage (Quest)#015.dst: 在 [-{~1}, {~2}, -{~3}] 附近尋找線索，並把 [{~} 古怪珠子] 帶回給 Ildan。

The Passage (Quest)#016.dst: 厲害！你把珠子拿到手了！
The Passage (Quest)#016.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#017.src: Well, welcome to this town, adventurer! You are now officially a citizen.
The Passage (Quest)#017.dst: 那麼，歡迎來到這個鎮，冒險者！你正式成為鎮民了。
The Passage (Quest)#017.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#018.src: Oh, but before you go! I do have a few things to say. First, about the beads here.
The Passage (Quest)#018.dst: 哦，不過在你走之前！我還有幾件事要說。第一，關於這裡的珠子。
The Passage (Quest)#018.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#019.src: The tribesmen accept these as currency, so if you collect enough, I've heard they can offer you powerful masks.
The Passage (Quest)#019.dst: 部落的人把這些當貨幣用，所以你要是收集得夠多，聽說他們可以給你強力的面具。
The Passage (Quest)#019.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#020.src: Second, about the shrine. Now, this is just a rumor, but apparently that tomb is not unique.
The Passage (Quest)#020.dst: 第二，關於那座神壇。這只是傳聞，但那座墓穴似乎不是唯一的一座。
The Passage (Quest)#020.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#021.src: There are supposed to be a bunch of these altars scattered around the province, even in Gavel too!
The Passage (Quest)#021.dst: 據說這種祭壇散布在整個行省，連 Gavel 那邊都有！
The Passage (Quest)#021.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#022.src: If true, you should look for them. While the fights will be tough, I would imagine great rewards could be gotten from them!
The Passage (Quest)#022.dst: 如果是真的，你應該去找找看。那些戰鬥會很硬，但我猜報酬也會很可觀！
The Passage (Quest)#022.speaker: Ildan

The Passage (Quest)#023.src: Anyway, I've talked enough. I'm proud to have such a powerful fighter join our town! I wish you luck, friend!
The Passage (Quest)#023.dst: 好了，我話說夠多了。有你這樣的強者加入我們鎮，我很驕傲！祝你好運，朋友！
The Passage (Quest)#023.speaker: Ildan

The Price of Ingenuity#000.src: Rest for the night in you room in the Steel Feather at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Price of Ingenuity#001.src: ...what. Where is it? W-where is it?!
The Price of Ingenuity#001.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#003.src: My bow, Yuman! Where is it? WHERE did you put it?!
The Price of Ingenuity#003.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#004.src: Hey, hey, relax, jeez! It's over here, on the meeting table! It fell off your bed in the early morning, so I figured I'd put it somewhere safe!
The Price of Ingenuity#004.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#005.src: I didn't, like, snatch it off ya or anything! Sorry, man! My bad. I forgot you got like this.
The Price of Ingenuity#005.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#007.src: Sorry. For shouting at you. I... don't know what came over me.
The Price of Ingenuity#007.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#008.src: Hey, it's all good! I get grouchy too when one of my bros moves my stuff without tellin' me! 'Kay, well, maybe not that grouchy, but- I sorta get it, is what I mean.
The Price of Ingenuity#008.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#009.src: Mmh. Did I ever tell you about it back when I was staying here?
The Price of Ingenuity#009.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#010.src: Nah, don't think you ever did. You were still keepin' everyone an arm's length away back then, so I didn't want to push my luck.
The Price of Ingenuity#010.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#011.src: Right... right. It's not even that big of a deal. My bow's just... important to me.
The Price of Ingenuity#011.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#012.src: Yes, I know I look silly walking around with the bulky thing all day! But I can't afford to lose it. I need it. I can't explain why, but I do.
The Price of Ingenuity#012.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#013.src: Nah that's cool, man! If we're talkin' silly, just take a look at me! I fight using my GUITAR! How d'you get sillier than that?
The Price of Ingenuity#013.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#014.src: Pff, ha! What, do you just play bad music until your enemies give up? "Please, stop, I can't bear it! The melody's too discordant!"
The Price of Ingenuity#014.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#015.src: Hahahah! That'd be fun, I should try that! But nah, I just club 'em with it. Yus stuck some metal plates in, so it hurts more and doesn't break!
The Price of Ingenuity#015.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#016.src: Wow. You're right, that's way sillier than what I do. I've got to tell Zeph about this.
The Price of Ingenuity#016.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#017.src: Woah, hey! You don't gotta do that, let him think I'm cool! But, uh, jokes aside. Feeling better?
The Price of Ingenuity#017.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#019.src: Good! Cool, then you should wake up the rest of your gang. Quill said he'd be over soon, wanted to talk to you about something.
The Price of Ingenuity#019.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#020.src: Wake up the other three members at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Price of Ingenuity#023.src: Morning, Sui! She's not exactly a... morning person. Guess I forgot to warn you!
The Price of Ingenuity#023.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#027.src: Why'd you wake me up? Um, this early.
The Price of Ingenuity#027.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#030.src: Um... is he... expecting me to, ha, prepare, breakfast? Oh, no...
The Price of Ingenuity#030.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#032.src: And there she goes. Well, no stopping her anxieties now! Might as well just let her get it out of her system.
The Price of Ingenuity#032.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#035.src: Ah, yes, I had overheard! I assume he has some work for us then.
The Price of Ingenuity#035.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#036.src: Allow me to go freshen up, and then I will join you.
The Price of Ingenuity#036.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#037.src: Surprisingly so, yes! These beds were much more comfortable than I had anticipated...
The Price of Ingenuity#037.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#038.src: However... hm. I appear to have been afflicted with repeating night terrors.
The Price of Ingenuity#038.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#039.src: Reality is setting in, in a sense. Returning to the {p} now is out of the question. We cannot come home until the deed is done.
The Price of Ingenuity#039.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#040.src: It does weigh on me a little. We have made new friends and allies here, but this is the furthest away I have ever been from home.
The Price of Ingenuity#040.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#041.src: Hm. I know the feeling, Mora. If it helps, it never really goes away, but it becomes... lighter. Easier to deal with.
The Price of Ingenuity#041.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#042.src: Hoho! It does not especially, no. But I appreciate the sentiment. I am glad to have my family here with me.
The Price of Ingenuity#042.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#043.src: But enough of that! I heard Quill was coming over? I had best freshen up before he arrives. I will join the rest of you later.
The Price of Ingenuity#043.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#045.src: Hrrk..... f-f-five more minutes, m- s- Synd- Zzzzzzzzz.....
The Price of Ingenuity#045.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#047.src: Okay, he's slept enough. What do you think, should I shoot him?
The Price of Ingenuity#047.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#048.src: Pfft! Ha, kidding. It wouldn't work anyway, he's stubborn enough to just roll over and keep sleeping.
The Price of Ingenuity#048.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#049.src: Hm, what can we try... oh, I know.
The Price of Ingenuity#049.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#050.src: Oh, wow, these sure are some nice and shiny and rare trinkets! Gosh, if only Zeph were awake, he'd love these. What a shame!
The Price of Ingenuity#050.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#051.src: HUH! N-no, wait, I- I- I'm awake, where are- sh-sh-show me the t-trinkets, I want to see-
The Price of Ingenuity#051.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#054.src: There aren't an-any tr-trinkets, are there.
The Price of Ingenuity#054.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#055.src: Nope! But I like the enthusiasm.
The Price of Ingenuity#055.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#056.src: Ugh... wh-why are you w-waking everyone up, anyway? I d-didn't think we had an-anything planned today..
The Price of Ingenuity#056.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#057.src: O-oh! Uh... I- I- I- I slept... fine. G-g-good, even! Yeah!
The Price of Ingenuity#057.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#059.src: H-hey! What's that s-s-supposed to mean!?
The Price of Ingenuity#059.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#060.src: You got in bed super late! And you know how I know that? Because your snoring only started waking me up after that!
The Price of Ingenuity#060.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#061.src: I kept waking up thinking it was thundering outside, that's how loud it was!
The Price of Ingenuity#061.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#062.src: Wh-what?! N-n-no, that's not- {u}, b-back me up here! I- I wasn't sn-snoring loudly, right?
The Price of Ingenuity#062.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#063.src: S-see! It couldn't have been th-that bad.
The Price of Ingenuity#063.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#064.src: Or maybe {u} needs to sleep lighter! Next thing you know, an enemy's gonna sneak up on you at night, and you're not gonna hear it because you're too used to Zeph's loud snoring!
The Price of Ingenuity#064.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#065.src: Oh my g-gods... the whole station m-must have heard me!
The Price of Ingenuity#065.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#066.src: It better have been just the station! Next thing you know, the crown's going to raid this hideout, and they would've only found it because your snoring echoes around {p} every night!
The Price of Ingenuity#066.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#068.src: Oh! W-wonder what it's about. Do you-
The Price of Ingenuity#068.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#069.src: Do you think h-he's mad about my mistake?
The Price of Ingenuity#069.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#070.src: You heard him yourself, stupid. He wasn't mad! He thinks you did the right thing!
The Price of Ingenuity#070.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#071.src: B-but... Still! Ugh. I'll have to go freshen up b-before he's here then!
The Price of Ingenuity#071.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#072.src: And that leaves one more. Hm...
The Price of Ingenuity#072.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#073.src: {u}, you should let me wake her.
The Price of Ingenuity#073.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#074.src: She's... kind of like Sui, but more intense? In the way she's, y'know. Military trained.
The Price of Ingenuity#074.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#075.src: So it's probably better if I do it since I know what I'm dealing with!
The Price of Ingenuity#075.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#077.src: You know, you'd think she'd wake up at the crack of dawn with her military background... but nope.
The Price of Ingenuity#077.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#081.src: I thought I'd be prepared for it, but nope...
The Price of Ingenuity#081.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#082.src: We thought you were asleep, Syndra! I was coming up to wake you!
The Price of Ingenuity#082.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#083.src: Well... I'm awake. Quill is stopping by, right?
The Price of Ingenuity#083.speaker: Syndra

The Price of Ingenuity#085.src: I've been awake for a while, Rex. I heard you talking about it downstairs!
The Price of Ingenuity#085.speaker: Syndra

The Price of Ingenuity#086.src: And here I thought I was a morning person...
The Price of Ingenuity#086.speaker: Syndra

The Price of Ingenuity#088.src: Ah, hello! Good morning to you all.
The Price of Ingenuity#088.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#090.src: Oh, dear. What is with all the formality this morning?
The Price of Ingenuity#090.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#091.src: Well, Yuman told us to be up and ready since you were coming-
The Price of Ingenuity#091.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#092.src: -so, naturally, the assumption was made that you had a mission for us-
The Price of Ingenuity#092.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#093.src: -o-o-or that w-we had done something wrong...
The Price of Ingenuity#093.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#096.src: Pahaha! Goodness, that was a lot all at once. Syndra, are they typically like this?
The Price of Ingenuity#096.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#097.src: They're not usually this snappy, no. But between meeting the brothers and experiencing the Roughworks, they're probably getting swept up in their emotions.
The Price of Ingenuity#097.speaker: Syndra

The Price of Ingenuity#098.src: Ah... I understand, don't worry. But no, I'm not here to assign you all a mission, nor to scold you, or anything else of the sort.
The Price of Ingenuity#098.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#099.src: I simply wanted to offer you all a starting sum of tickets for the shops. I'd meant to give them yesterday, but in the chaos I forgot to.
The Price of Ingenuity#099.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#100.src: The ticket system is used to ration out food and other items to people that need it. You'll receive a weekly allowance of tickets to spend on whatever you'd like, in addition to this starting sum.
The Price of Ingenuity#100.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#101.src: Of course, basic amenities are free of charge if you're part of our community. Wouldn't want any of our members to sleep on the tracks, after all!
The Price of Ingenuity#101.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#102.src: So... I baked bread for, um, no reason?
The Price of Ingenuity#102.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#103.src: I fear so, haha! Do not worry, you will not be forced to do work here.
The Price of Ingenuity#103.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#104.src: And, besides, if I wanted you to cook for us, I would have let you know well in advance.
The Price of Ingenuity#104.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#105.src: I mean... I w-wouldn't mind some fr-fresh bread...
The Price of Ingenuity#105.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#107.src: Ah, one more thing. I wanted to point you all towards the training yard- Zeph, I believe you have been there already?
The Price of Ingenuity#107.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#109.src: I believe the brothers should be there right now. If you're to be working with us, it would be best to get used to each other's fighting styles.
The Price of Ingenuity#109.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#110.src: Why don't you go join them there, while Syndra and I discuss further matters?
The Price of Ingenuity#110.speaker: Quill

The Price of Ingenuity#111.src: Find the brothers at the training yard at [-{~}, {~}, -{~}].

The Price of Ingenuity#112.src: ...do you really gotta head out there again?
The Price of Ingenuity#112.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#113.src: You know contracts are rare, man. I have to take what I can get.
The Price of Ingenuity#113.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#114.src: Why's it always gotta be you and Yus heading out?! For once- for once, man, take care of yourself!
The Price of Ingenuity#114.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#118.src: No, this can wait. Did Quill send you over?
The Price of Ingenuity#118.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#119.src: Indeed he did. He suggested we get to know each other's fighting styles!
The Price of Ingenuity#119.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#120.src: Not a bad idea. Yuman and I would be happy to show off what we can do, right?
The Price of Ingenuity#120.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#122.src: Well, Zeph, {u}, and I've already been through it! Some cool moves from you both! Man, getting to see a cursed one in action was awesome...
The Price of Ingenuity#122.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#124.src: Yeah! Like, I'd hear all the stories, and think... man, having those kinds of powers sounds so cool. Sometimes I wished I could have em! Without, uh, being evil, of course.
The Price of Ingenuity#124.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#125.src: You'd be even harder to deal with if you did, bro. But on that subject- Quill said something about you all practicing... what was the word he used... "magic?"
The Price of Ingenuity#125.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#126.src: What?! Ey, princess, why didn't you show anything off the other day?
The Price of Ingenuity#126.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#128.src: Don't be insensitive, Yuman. It isn't something people just... pick up.
The Price of Ingenuity#128.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#129.src: From what little I've heard from Quill, it can take years of study to master a blessing... so I wouldn't be surprised if they couldn't even make a spark! Uh, no offense.
The Price of Ingenuity#129.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#130.src: W- well... maybe we'll s- sur- surprise you!
The Price of Ingenuity#130.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#131.src: Ha, think you're the only ones with hidden talents? I've got a trick or two up my sleeve too!
The Price of Ingenuity#131.speaker: Yusanu

The Price of Ingenuity#133.src: It's an expression, dumbass. Like you're one to talk. Why are you half-naked?
The Price of Ingenuity#133.speaker: Yusanu

The Price of Ingenuity#134.src: To show off my abs? Obviously. Anyway, {u}, why don't you decide who goes first?
The Price of Ingenuity#134.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#136.src: Who, me? Sorry, but I'll sit this one out until you're all done.
The Price of Ingenuity#136.speaker: Yusanu

The Price of Ingenuity#137.src: Got to save the best for last, right? Heh.
The Price of Ingenuity#137.speaker: Yusanu

The Price of Ingenuity#138.src: I'll have to add arrows until my bowstring runs out of space next time...
The Price of Ingenuity#138.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#139.src: I'll h-have to come back here a-again tonight!
The Price of Ingenuity#139.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#140.src: It's like there's ripples gently spreading within me...
The Price of Ingenuity#140.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#141.src: To see my powers growing this clearly...
The Price of Ingenuity#141.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#143.src: Dang, I think I overloaded it. I'll have to put it through a charge cycle...
The Price of Ingenuity#143.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#145.src: So. Magic, curses, blessings... whatever you want to call it, it hasn't worked for me. It just doesn't... click.
The Price of Ingenuity#145.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#146.src: Ah, not to worry, Rex! Even without it, none in the province could match your accuracy with a bow.
The Price of Ingenuity#146.speaker: Mora

The Price of Ingenuity#147.src: Y- yeah! And if you d- did get magic, it'd j- jus- just be unfair for the rest of us!
The Price of Ingenuity#147.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#148.src: Yeah, yeah, sure. Either way, I've been practicing a new technique... let's see if I can pull it off.
The Price of Ingenuity#148.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#150.src: Yep! I just place every arrow on the string at once, which lets me shoot at a much larger area!
The Price of Ingenuity#150.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#151.src: But... how'd you manage to hit each arrow right on target?! That's... insane!
The Price of Ingenuity#151.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#152.src: Ha. Go on, keep praising my skill. That was actually the first time I tried that many arrows at once... glad it worked out!
The Price of Ingenuity#152.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#153.src: The... first... You said you'd practiced it, man! What do you mean that was the first time?!
The Price of Ingenuity#153.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#154.src: Yeah? I practiced theoretically. In my head. Keep up, Yulie.
The Price of Ingenuity#154.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#156.src: Couldn't even make a spark, eh?
The Price of Ingenuity#156.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#157.src: Alright, alright! I've been proven wrong.
The Price of Ingenuity#157.speaker: Yulie

The Price of Ingenuity#159.src: So... I w-want to first say that I've been c-coming here every night.
The Price of Ingenuity#159.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#160.src: I was e-embarrassed that I just didn't g-get it.
The Price of Ingenuity#160.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#161.src: I mean, j-just look at how fast your m-magic developed, Mora!
The Price of Ingenuity#161.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#162.src: And you, S-sui! You are a natural, a-after all.
The Price of Ingenuity#162.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#163.src: I still don't know any form of magic. Why feel so embarassed?
The Price of Ingenuity#163.speaker: Rex

The Price of Ingenuity#164.src: Rex, you don't even n-need magic to be a valuable asset! You're the best archer in the w-world!
The Price of Ingenuity#164.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#165.src: I don't h-have that skill! My blade skills a-aren't good enough! You've h-had to save me time and time a-again.
The Price of Ingenuity#165.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#166.src: And {u}, I felt like I had l-let you down after all the k-knowledge you had given me.
The Price of Ingenuity#166.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#167.src: I may not have talked to you a lot, Zeph. But from what I know of the science behind magic, you don't have to blame yourself for not getting it.
The Price of Ingenuity#167.speaker: Yusanu

The Price of Ingenuity#168.src: A lot of people study magic their whole lives. I'm sure you'll get there eventually.
The Price of Ingenuity#168.speaker: Yusanu

The Price of Ingenuity#169.src: Thank y-you, Yusanu. However, I think I f-finally figured it out...
The Price of Ingenuity#169.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#171.src: I think I'm finally g-getting this magic thing somewhat down!
The Price of Ingenuity#171.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#172.src: I will n-not stop practicing! N-not until I can m-m-match you all!
The Price of Ingenuity#172.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#174.src: Come on, man! Show us what you've got!
The Price of Ingenuity#174.speaker: Yuman

The Price of Ingenuity#175.src: ...okay. I've tried to, um, practice a bit, now that I'm... yeah.
The Price of Ingenuity#175.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#176.src: I haven't fully developed it, but, I have this new skill...
The Price of Ingenuity#176.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#177.src: Okay! I'm going to try it!
The Price of Ingenuity#177.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#178.src: W- woah! It's like you ma- made that out of n- n- nothing!
The Price of Ingenuity#178.speaker: Zeph

The Price of Ingenuity#179.src: ...ugh! It takes so much concentration... even a word makes me fail...
The Price of Ingenuity#179.speaker: Sui

The Price of Ingenuity#180.src: Also. It's not, um, out of nothing.
The Price of Ingenuity#180.speaker: Sui
